input.content:
# Places

One entity per place on Earth that any framework we use gives a code to, with
a generated profile that joins everything the other topology folders already
map. Built 2026-11-05, cheaply and deterministically: 31 small downloads
(13 MB of pins), no model in the build, byte-identical on rerun.

Sloane Ortel: "we have a set that is countries, so we should have all the
countries on there... thinking about the world as a connected set of entities
with non-homogeneous concerns... if we're going to cover topologies, we
should cover topologies."

## The principle

**"Place" is a placeholder.** It stands in for the entity type until Sloane
chooses the word. The folder is still named `countries/`. Nothing here uses a
word that ranks one kind of place above another, because, in her words, "If
we can't call Taiwan a country, we're not going to call anything a country,
and we're just going to use a different word for it."

**Identity is not decided by whoever issues the documents.** Sloane: "as a
trans person, is it really the case that your identity should be tied to the
people who issue your documents?" So:

- **ISO 3166 codes are keys for joining tables, not judgments.** Every place
  also has our own `place_id`, minted once in `place-ids.tsv` and never
  renumbered, so a place can exist here without any ISO code (three already
  do).
- **There is no status column.** Recognition is something a framework asserts
  about a place, not a property of the place. `framework-membership.tsv`
  records, per place and per framework, how that framework treats it, in the
  framework's own terms ("Sovereign country", "Disputed" and "Indeterminate"
  are Natural Earth's words).
- **How a place describes itself** belongs in `self_description`, quoted from
  its own government or representative body. It is blank for every place: no
  such page has been pinned yet. It is never inferred.
- **Our own values are recorded separately** from any framework's treatment.
  This folder records none yet. When it does, they get their own table, and
  they never edit a framework row.

## Files

| file | what it is | kind |
|---|---|---|
| `places.tsv` | 260 places: `place_id`, `iso2`, `iso3`, `iso_numeric`, CLDR English name, region and subregion (CLDR containment, which uses M49 codes), Natural Earth key, `self_description` | computed |
| `place-ids.tsv` | our id registry: `place_id`, the source key it was minted from | computed once, then fixed |
| `framework-membership.tsv` | 1,550 rows: (place, framework, treatment, evidence, pin) | computed |
| `indicators.tsv` | long table: place, indicator, value, year, source, pin | computed |
| `indicator-coverage.tsv` | per indicator: definition, unit, licence, places with a value / 260, years | computed |
| `links.tsv` | per place: rows in other topology folders carrying its ISO alpha-2 code | computed |
| `leaving-america.tsv` | frontmatter of the guide's 27 destination pages, with commit and blob SHA | computed |
| `question-set.in.tsv` / `question-set.tsv` | 20 questions generalised from the guide, each with a verbatim source line | **proposal** |
| `question-coverage.tsv` | per question: proposed indicator and how many places have a value | computed from the proposal |
| `profiles/<place_id>.md`, `profiles/index.tsv` | one short page per place | computed |
| `targets.tsv`, `MANIFEST.tsv`, `terms.tsv`, `sources.tsv` | what we tried to fetch, what was pinned, licence clauses, per-source verdicts | as in every topology folder |
| `scripts/pin.py` | thin wrapper over `../scripts/topo.py` (the gate) | |
| `scripts/build.py` | stdlib, PEP 723: every computed file above from the pins (`check` fails on any byte difference) | |
| `scripts/leaving_america.py` | `extract` / `verify` the guide frontmatter and question quotes (read-only on Dark) | |
| `scripts/question_set.py` | adds blob SHA and quote SHA-256 to the question set; fails if a quote is not a whole source line | |

Rebuild: `uv run scripts/pin.py pin`, `uv run scripts/build.py`,
`uv run scripts/leaving_america.py extract`, `uv run scripts/question_set.py`,
then `uv run scripts/build.py` again (profiles read the Leaving America tables).
Check: `uv run scripts/pin.py verify`, `uv run scripts/build.py check`,
`uv run scripts/leaving_america.py verify`.

## Sources and terms

Every fetch went through the gate (`../scripts/topo.py`): terms page first,
verdict recorded in `sources.tsv`, `gate build`, then content. robots.txt
honoured; no key, email or other identifier sent.

| source | used for | licence (clause in `terms.tsv`) | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unicode CLDR 47 | codes, English names, containment, UN grouping | Unicode License v3 | open |
| Natural Earth 1:50m admin-0, v5.1.2 | its TYPE per feature; the three places with no ISO code | public domain | open |
| World Bank WDI API and country list | population, GDP per capita PPP, electricity access, inflation, PM2.5; WB listing | CC BY 4.0 | open |
| UNDP HDR 2025 time series; global MPI 2026 Table 1 | HDI, MPI; HDR listing | CC BY 3.0 IGO | open |
| Ember via Our World in Data | grid carbon intensity, renewables share | Ember CC BY 4.0; OWID processing CC BY | open |
| V-Dem via Our World in Data | electoral democracy index | **CC BY-SA 4.0**: tables carrying these values inherit share-alike | open |
| UN M49 overview | inclusion flag only | UN terms (non-commercial; `../ai-centers/sources.tsv`) | redistribution-barred: read locally; only "listed, code N" is committed |

**Not fetched, recorded:** Equaldex (website terms bar public display; API
needs a registered key): `licence-required`, refused. ILGA World Database:
no terms found, `unverified`, refused. Wikidata Query Service and the
Wikidata API: robots.txt disallows them for our User-Agent (fetchlog rows
`wd-places`, `wd-api-sample`), and item pages run to megabytes each. So
**Wikidata instance-of classes are missing** from the framework table. **UN
observer status** is also missing: the UN's own pages list members by name,
with no codes, and a name join would need judgement. Ember's own yearly CSV
exceeds the 20 MB fetch cap, hence the OWID copy.

**Where the M49 terms were avoided:** regions come from CLDR, which
redistributes the M49 hierarchy under its own licence. Taiwan and Kosovo are
present (CLDR gives TW, and XK in the user-assigned range); M49 lists
neither, and that fact is a row in `framework-membership.tsv`.

## Coverage (places with a value / 260)

Population 216; GDP per capita PPP 199; electricity access 214; inflation 190;
PM2.5 200; HDI 193; MPI 107 (a developing-economies table; one name,
"Naoero", did not match exactly and is left unjoined); grid carbon intensity
212; renewables share 212; V-Dem 174. A value older than 2015 is shown as
missing rather than carried forward (V-Dem gives the Holy See 1870 as its latest year).

**Links** (explicit ISO alpha-2 only; `intl`, `EU` and blank codes excluded):
bodies 118 rows over 38 places; AI-centers works 42,027 over 162 places and
1,248 institutions over 97; benefit claims 74 over 8 (24 actors); asset owners
46 over 17; training-method uses 101 over 8 (33 developers); Norway bodies 3.
Norway's `decisions.tsv` has no code column, so it is not linked.
`asset-owners/owners.tsv` is being written by another session, so its count
moves with that file.

**Question set:** 20 questions. 5 have a proposed open indicator: 2 bear
directly (inflation, PM2.5) and 3 partially (V-Dem for political order, HDI
for health care, GDP per capita PPP for cost). 15 have no open source.

## Computed and proposed

Computed: every table built from pins, the Leaving America frontmatter, and
the quote and blob hashes. Proposed (witness `llm:claude-opus-5-5
prompt=unrecorded`): the generalised wording of each question, which
indicator bears on it, and whether that bearing is direct or partial. The
quotes are checked; the readings are not.

## What this does not answer

- **A profile is not a recommendation.** It does not rank places or say
  where anyone should live or put compute.
- **Every indicator is an average over a whole place.** Inside every place,
  concerns differ by region, city, class, race, gender and sexuality, and a
  national figure hides all of that. The Leaving America guide reports cities
  for this reason.
- **No measure of safety by identity.** The open sources we found do not
  permit it (see above). A blank is not a finding of safety.
- **Pairwise questions** (totalization agreements, tax treaties, travel time,
  advisories) depend on where a person comes from. The guide answers them for
  the US only, and so does `leaving-america.tsv`.
- **Framework rows are assertions, not facts about the place.**

212; renewables share 212; V-Dem 174. A value older than 2015 is shown as
missing rather than carried forward (V-Dem gives the Holy See 1870 as its latest year).

**Links** (explicit ISO alpha-2 only; `intl`, `EU` and blank codes excluded):
bodies 118 rows over 38 places; AI-centers works 42,027 over 162 places and
1,248 institutions over 97; benefit claims 74 over 8 (24 actors); asset owners
46 over 17; training-method uses 101 over 8 (33 developers); Norway bodies 3.
Norway's `decisions.tsv` has no code column, so it is not linked.
`asset-owners/owners.tsv` is being written by another session, so its count
moves with that file.

**Question set:** 20 questions. 5 have a proposed open indicator: 2 bear
directly (inflation, PM2.5) and 3 partially (V-Dem for political order, HDI
for health care, GDP per capita PPP for cost). 15 have no open source.

Computed: every table built from pins, the Leaving America frontmatter, and
the quote and blob hashes. Proposed (witness `llm:claude-opus-5-5
prompt=unrecorded`): the generalised wording of each question, which
indicator bears on it, and whether that bearing is direct or partial. The
quotes are checked; the readings are not.

## What this does not answer

- **A profile is not a recommendation.** It does not rank places or say
  where anyone should live or put compute.
- **Every indicator is an average over a whole place.** Inside every place,
  concerns differ by region, city, class, race, gender and sexuality, and a
  national figure hides all of that. The Leaving America guide reports cities
  for this reason.
- **No measure of safety by identity.** The open sources we found do not
  permit it (see above). A blank is not a finding of safety.
- **Pairwise questions** (totalization agreements, tax treaties, travel time,
  advisories) depend on where a person comes from. The guide answers them for
  the US only, and so does `leaving-america.tsv`.
- **Framework rows are assertions, not facts about the place.**

**Rule breaks and edits outside the folder.** I made one edit to `scripts/topo.py`: the single FOLDERS registration line `"countries": {"cache": ".cache", "fetched": "2026-11-05"}`. I also ran `topo.py gate build`, which regenerated the derived `gate.tsv` at the topologies root (+7 scopes, one evidence line extended). That's the gate's required procedure, but strictly it's a write outside `countries/`. I ran no git writes in praxis. I read Dark only (`git show/ls-tree/cat-file` at cad2f33).

**Sloane's design change is applied.** The entity term is `place` and the README flags it as a placeholder. ISO codes are normalisation keys only. Every place has our own `place_id`, minted once in `place-ids.tsv`. There is no status column; `framework-membership.tsv` holds each framework's treatment instead. A `self_description` column exists but is blank for every place: nothing has been pinned from any place's own government yet.

**Entity set:** 260 places. 257 come from CLDR 47 territories (Unicode licence; regions come from CLDR, so the M49 terms aren't relied on). 3 come from Natural Earth features that have no ISO code (Somaliland, Northern Cyprus, Siachen). Taiwan and Kosovo are both present.

**Framework membership:** 1,550 rows covering:
- the ISO codes as CLDR carries them
- CLDR's UN grouping
- whether M49 lists the place (flag only, because the M49 terms bar redistribution)
- Natural Earth's TYPE, in its own words
- the World Bank list, with its region and income level
- whether UNDP's HDR lists the place

Wikidata's instance-of classes are missing: robots.txt disallows the Query Service, `api.php`, `rest.php` and `EntityData`. UN observer status is missing too: the UN lists members by name only, with no codes.

**Indicator coverage (places with a value, of 260; values older than 2015 shown as missing):**

| Indicator | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Population | 216 |
| GDP per capita PPP | 199 |
| Electricity access | 214 |
| Inflation | 190 |
| PM2.5 | 200 |
| HDI | 193 |
| MPI | 107 (one name, "Naoero", not joined) |
| Grid carbon intensity (Ember via OWID) | 212 |
| Renewables share (Ember via OWID) | 212 |
| V-Dem electoral democracy (via OWID) | 174 |

V-Dem is CC BY-SA, so tables carrying its values inherit share-alike. Equaldex is refused: its terms bar public display and its API needs a key. ILGA has no terms we could find, so it stays unverified and refused.

**Links (explicit alpha-2 codes only):**
- bodies: 118 rows over 38 places
- AI-centers: 42,027 works over 162 places; 1,248 institutions over 97
- benefit claims: 74 over 8 places
- asset owners: 46 over 17 (`owners.tsv` appeared mid-run; this count will move with that file)
- training-method uses: 101 over 8
- Norway bodies: 3 (Norway's `decisions.tsv` has no code column, so it isn't linked)

**Leaving America:** all 27 destination pages are in `leaving-america.tsv`, with blob SHAs; every name matched a place. `question-set.tsv` has 20 questions, each quoting one whole verbatim source line. 5 have a proposed open indicator: 2 bear directly (inflation, PM2.5) and 3 partially (V-Dem, HDI, GDP per capita PPP). 15 have no open source. The wording and the indicator mapping are proposals (witness `llm:claude-opus-5-5 prompt=unrecorded`).

**Files**, all under `/Users/srvo/dev/praxis/resources/topologies/countries/`:
- `places.tsv`, `place-ids.tsv`, `framework-membership.tsv`, `indicators.tsv`, `indicator-coverage.tsv`, `links.tsv`
- `leaving-america.tsv`, `question-set{.in,}.tsv`, `question-coverage.tsv`
- `profiles/` (260 pages plus `index.tsv`, 2.0 MB)
- `README.md`, `sources.tsv`, `terms.tsv` (11 verbatim clauses), `targets.tsv`, `MANIFEST.tsv` (30 pins)
- `scripts/{build,leaving_america,question_set,pin}.py`

The tables total about 392 KB. The pins in `.cache/` are 13 MB and gitignored.

**Determinism:** `build.py check` reports 0 differences. Deleting `profiles/` and rebuilding gave the same tree hash. `pin.py verify` passes (30 pins, 11 clauses, 0 problems), `gate check` is ok, `leaving_america.py verify` finds 0 problems, and `test_topo.py` passes 23/23. The one thing that will move between builds is the asset-owners count, while the other session writes `owners.tsv`.
